predecessors.note: Cao Cao died on 15 March 220 and 'his vassal king title was inherited by his son'; Cao Pi took the throne on 11 December. Cliopatria's Cao Cao row runs to 223 and its Cao Wei row begins in 224: 220-223 is the keyframe cao-wei_220.

successors.note: Cliopatria ends the Wei row in 264 and starts its Western Jin row in 265, a year or two before the page's 266.

rulers.note: Dec 220 - Jun 226 (infobox); forced Emperor Xian to abdicate on 11 December 220.

rulers.note: Jun 226 - Jan 239 (infobox); the page's rulers table gives 227-239, unreconciled.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Cao Wei row begins in 224, but the state was founded on 11 December 220 ('The state was established in 220 AD by Cao Pi based upon the foundations laid by his father Cao Cao'). 220-223 is the Cao Cao realm Cliopatria runs to 223 under the Cao Cao name, without the Gongsun land and without Hanzhong (lost to Liu Bei in 219) and without the Tarim, which the Chief Official post covers from 224 in Cliopatria's shape.

correction.text: Cliopatria's Cao Wei shape of 224 without the Gongsun land (until 238) and without the Western Regions (a vassal tint); holds 224-237

keyframe_review.note: 2,078,163 km2 (9,325 cells) for 224-237. Two corrections. (1) 657 cells (North Korea, Liaodong, Jilin) are the Gongsun land, Wei's only from September 238: 'Liaodong ... had been firmly rooted under Gongsun control for 4 decades' (page); Gongsun Yuan is Administrator of Liaodong from 228 under Cao Rui and 'Duke of Lelang' in 234 (Gongsun Yuan page). (2) The 2,266 Xinjiang and 125 Kyrgyz cells are the Western Regions, where the page opened says only that the Chief Official office was 'subsequently re-established and maintained by the Cao Wei and the Western Jin until around 328': an office, not a province, so a vassal tint (rule 4). Hexi, Gansu, Hebei and the rest stand. The page gives no infobox area (population 4,432,881 in 260).

correction.text: Cliopatria's Cao Wei shape of 238, which holds Liaodong and northwest Korea, without the Western Regions (a vassal tint); holds 238-262

keyframe_review.note: 2,092,804 km2 for 238-262: the 224 shape plus 81 cells. From September 238 the Gongsun land is Wei's: 'Liaodong and present-day northwest Korea became Wei territories'. The Western Regions are drawn as a vassal as above.

keyframe_review.note: 2,972,911 km2 (12,952 cells) for 263-264: the 238 shape plus Shu (Yi Province, Hanzhong, Nanzhong), conquered in autumn 263 ('Cao Wei victory; Fall of Shu Han'). The Cliopatria Western Jin row of 265 is the same shape (12,951 cells); the page ends Wei on 4 February 266, so this shape holds 263-265. 2.97 M km2 against 3.1 M km2 for the whole Jin of 280 (Jin page infobox) shows the Tarim cells inflate it.

region.text: the Han realm Cao Pi took in December 220: Cliopatria's Cao Cao shape of 215 without the Gongsun land and Hanzhong

ledger.note: 220: Cao Pi founds the Wei. 'The state was established in 220 AD by Cao Pi'; 'on 11 December, Cao Pi forced Emperor Xian to abdicate in his favour'. The seat is Xuchang. The page names no boundary: the land is the Cao Cao realm.

region.text: Sun Quan's domain in 221: Jiangdong and Jing, without Jiao and Guang

ledger.note: 221: Sun Quan becomes King of Wu under Wei. 'On 23 September 221, Cao Pi appointed Sun Quan King of Wu. Cao Pi had earlier made Sun a Wei vassal.' (The Eastern Wu page dates the title to 220.) The extent is Wu's domain of the time, my reading.

region.text: the Wei-Wu frontier from Jiangling to the lower Yangtze and the Huai

ledger.note: 222: Wei attacks Wu. 'On its southern and eastern borders, Wei engaged Wu in a series of armed conflicts throughout the 220s and 230s'; the battles listed are Dongkou (222-223), Jiangling (223) and Shiting (228). The page names no places beyond the battles; the Huai-Yangtze frontier is a band of the two Cliopatria shapes of 224.

region.text: Sun Quan's domain in 221: Jiangdong and Jing, without Jiao and Guang

ledger.note: 222: Sun Quan breaks with Wei. 'In November 222, Sun declared independence by changing the era name, after refusing Cao Pi's demand for his son Sun Deng as a hostage.' (Three Kingdoms page: 'Sun Quan declares Wu independent of Wei'; Cao Wei infobox 'Eastern Wu declaring independence from Wei: 222'.)

region.text: the Wei-Wu frontier from Jiangling to the lower Yangtze and the Huai

ledger.note: 223: the Dongkou and Jiangling battles end without a change of frontier.

region.text: the Western Regions: the Tarim Basin and the Kyrgyz edge that Cliopatria's Wei and Jin shapes reach (73 E)

ledger.note: 224: the Western Regions as a Wei dependency. The Chief Official of the Western Regions 'was subsequently re-established and maintained by the Cao Wei and the Western Jin until around 328', but the page gives no year for Wei's re-establishment; 224 is the year Cliopatria's Cao Wei shape first reaches 73 E. The Cao Wei page opened is silent on the Western Regions.
226: the capital moves from Xuchang to Luoyang (infobox: Xuchang 220-226, Luoyang 226-266).

region.text: the Gongsun land: Liaodong, Xuantu, Lelang and Daifang (North Korea, eastern Liaoning, Jilin)

ledger.note: 228: Gongsun Yuan holds Liaodong under Wei. Infobox: 'Administrator of Liaodong: in office 228 to ?; monarch Cao Rui', after seizing power from his uncle Gongsun Gong in 228; in the twelfth month of Qinglong 1 (18 January to 15 February 234) he was 'appointed da sima and Duke of Lelang'. The Gongsun had held Liaodong, Xuantu, Lelang and Daifang since the late Han.

region.text: the Wei front north of Hanzhong in Longyou, where Zhuge Liang's expeditions fought

ledger.note: 228: Zhuge Liang's northern expeditions begin. 'Between 228 and 234, Zhuge Liang, the Shu chancellor and regent, led a series of five military campaigns'.

region.text: the Wei-Wu frontier from Jiangling to the lower Yangtze and the Huai

ledger.note: 228: the battle of Shiting on the Wu front, listed among the Wei-Wu battles (Dongkou 222-223, Jiangling 223, Shiting 228).

region.text: the Wei-Wu frontier from Jiangling to the lower Yangtze and the Huai

ledger.note: 228: Shiting ends without a change of frontier.

region.text: the Wei front north of Hanzhong in Longyou, where Zhuge Liang's expeditions fought

ledger.note: 234: Zhuge Liang dies at the Wuzhang Plains and the expeditions end.

region.text: the Gongsun land: Liaodong, Xuantu, Lelang and Daifang (North Korea, eastern Liaoning, Jilin)

ledger.note: 237: Gongsun Yuan rebels. 'Gongsun Yuan declared himself "King of Yan" and concluded an alliance with Eastern Wu' (infobox: King of Yan, 237 to c. September 238).

region.text: the Gongsun land: Liaodong, Xuantu, Lelang and Daifang (North Korea, eastern Liaoning, Jilin)

ledger.note: 238: Sima Yi marches on Liaodong. 'It was Sima Yi who, in June 238, as the Grand Commandant, launched an invasion with 40,000 troops'.

region.text: the Gongsun land: Liaodong, Xuantu, Lelang and Daifang (North Korea, eastern Liaoning, Jilin)

ledger.note: 238: Wei takes Liaodong and northwest Korea. Sima Yi laid siege to Xiangping on 3 September 238 (footnote) and 'Gongsun Yuan was defeated and killed while his clan was exterminated'; 'Liaodong and present-day northwest Korea became Wei territories.' (Three Kingdoms page: 'Sima Yi defeats Gongsun Yuan's Yan Kingdom, bringing Liaodong under Wei control'.) The Lelang page gives 236 for the annexation of Liaodong, Lelang and Daifang, a slip.

region.text: the Gongsun land: Liaodong, Xuantu, Lelang and Daifang (North Korea, eastern Liaoning, Jilin)

ledger.note: September 238: Xiangping falls; the Zizhi Tongjian places the fall on 19 September 238 (footnote).

region.text: Hwando, Goguryeo's capital on the Yalu

ledger.note: 244: Wei reaches Hwando. 'Goguryeo initiated the Goguryeo-Wei Wars in 242'; 'Hwando was destroyed in a reprisal raid by Wei forces in 244' (Three Kingdoms page: 'Guanqiu Jian invades Goguryeo and devastates it', 244-245).

region.text: Hwando, Goguryeo's capital on the Yalu

ledger.note: 245: Guanqiu Jian's raid ends; Wei holds no Goguryeo land.

region.text: Yi Province and Hanzhong, the ground of the invasion of Shu

ledger.note: 263: Wei invades Shu. 'In the autumn of 263, the Wei imperial court issued an edict outlining a three-pronged invasion of Shu'; the armies left Luoyang between 20 September and 19 October.

region.text: all of Shu: Yi Province, Hanzhong and Nanzhong

ledger.note: 263: Wei conquers Shu. 'In 263, Wei armies led by Zhong Hui and Deng Ai conquered Shu.' Liu Shan surrendered to Deng Ai at Chengdu in November or December; the Hanzhong and Yinping routes were taken first. Deng Ai appointed Shi Zuan Inspector of Yi Province.

region.text: Yi Province and Hanzhong, the ground of the invasion of Shu

ledger.note: December 263: the war ends with the surrender of Chengdu; Zhong Hui's mutiny at Chengdu (1-3 March 264) is the aftermath.

region.text: the Western Regions: the Tarim Basin and the Kyrgyz edge that Cliopatria's Wei and Jin shapes reach (73 E)

ledger.note: 266: the Western Regions pass with the throne to the Western Jin, which the same page names as the office's second holder ('maintained by the Cao Wei and the Western Jin'); the year is the dynasty's.

region.text: the whole Wei realm with Shu

ledger.note: 266: Sima Yan ends the Wei. 'On 4 February 266, Sima Zhao's son, Sima Yan, forced Cao Huan to abdicate in his favor'; the Jin dynasty begins. (Sima Zhao had died on 6 September 265.)

wars.name: Wei-Wu border wars of the 220s

zones.text: the Wei-Wu frontier from Jiangling to the lower Yangtze and the Huai

wars.outcome: Battles at Dongkou (222-223), Jiangling (223) and Shiting (228); no change of frontier.
wars.note: Later Wei-Wu fighting at Shouchun: 'In 258, Sima Zhao quelled Zhuge Dan's rebellion, marking an end to what are known as the Three Rebellions in Shouchun'; the page gives no other dates.

wars.name: Zhuge Liang's Northern Expeditions

zones.text: the Wei front north of Hanzhong in Longyou, where Zhuge Liang's expeditions fought

wars.outcome: Five Shu campaigns without lasting gain.

wars.name: Sima Yi's Liaodong campaign

zones.text: the Gongsun land: Liaodong, Xuantu, Lelang and Daifang (North Korea, eastern Liaoning, Jilin)

wars.outcome: Gongsun Yuan's Yan is destroyed in September 238 and Liaodong and northwest Korea become Wei's.
wars.note: Sima Yi's invasion in June 238 (Wei page); siege of Xiangping 3 September, fall about 19 September (Gongsun Yuan page footnotes).

wars.name: Goguryeo-Wei Wars

zones.text: Hwando, Goguryeo's capital on the Yalu

wars.outcome: Wei destroys Hwando in 244; Guanqiu Jian's raid of 244-245 leaves no Wei garrison.

wars.name: Conquest of Shu by Wei

zones.text: Yi Province and Hanzhong, the ground of the invasion of Shu

wars.outcome: Shu is annexed; Wu's relief attacks of January-March 264 are withdrawn.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a border. The Western Regions are a dependency without a line; the frontier with Wu runs along the Huai and the Yangtze and with Shu along the Qinling at Hanzhong, all approximate.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROWS. Cao Wei has three shapes (224-237, 238-262, 263-264). Wikidata Q320930 is shared with the Warring States state of Wei (slug wei): a Wikidata mislink, different states; not merged. Cao Wei starts 11 December 220, four years before Cliopatria's 224; 220-223 is drawn by Cliopatria's Cao Cao row, here the new keyframe cao-wei_220 (the cao-cao dossier ends in December 220). Cliopatria's Han Dynasty row runs to 237 and is marked wrong by the han-dynasty dossier.
CORRECTIONS. (1) The Gongsun land (657 cells of the 224 shape: Liaodong, Xuantu, Lelang, Daifang) is subtracted until September 238 and recorded as a vassal 228-237 (Gongsun Yuan, Administrator of Liaodong from 228, Duke of Lelang 234); Cliopatria draws it as Wei land from 207. (2) The Western Regions (2,266 Xinjiang and 125 Kyrgyz cells) are taken out of the shape and recorded as a vassal of the Chief Official office, whose only support is one sentence on a thin page, and whose start year 224 is Cliopatria's (confidence 1). (3) The 263 shape holds 263-265 and the Wei dissolves on 4 February 266.
GAPS. The Wei page gives no area, no Western Regions detail, no Ye, no Gongsun, no Wuhuan or Xianbei detail; the Xianbei under Kebineng (Cliopatria's Xianbei row ends 237, a neighbour of the Wei 224-237) were not read. Wei's frontier with Wu at Hefei, Shouchun and Xiangyang rests on battle names only (Dongkou 222-223, Jiangling 223, Shiting 228). The Zhong Hui mutiny at Chengdu (1-3 March 264) was not drawn.
DISAGREEMENTS. Sun Quan's King of Wu title: 23 September 221 (Sun Quan page) against 220 (Eastern Wu page). Rulers: the infobox (Cao Rui 226-239) and the rulers table (227-239, Cao Fang 240-249) disagree. The Lelang Commandery page dates Sima Yi's annexation of Liaodong, Lelang and Daifang to 236; the Cao Wei, Three Kingdoms and Gongsun Yuan pages say 238. Conquest of Shu page: the surrender is in the 18 November to 17 December window.
COUNTERPARTS. gongsun-liaodong, goguryeo, eastern-wu, shu-han and protectorate-of-the-western-regions have dossiers (other groups). The Xianbei, Wuhuan and Dongye frontier events are not covered.
